subject: Partial generation suppression observed in hosted /v1/generate — customer report and interim advisory
messages:
From: Sana Patel <sana@novacredit.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 4 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected truncation / token suppression in production (novacredit-prod)

Hi Alex / Laura,

We started seeing partial responses from /v1/generate for several user flows starting ~08:50 PDT. The prompt appears to be accepted and the call returns 200, but the generated text ends abruptly mid-sentence in ~40% of calls. This is customer-impacting (billing & UX).

Examples attached (server-log-snippet.txt) and a curl trace. We are on the hosted plan; requests spike around 08:45 with a brief burst, then the symptom shows up. Can you confirm whether this is a client-side change or something on your side?

We need ETA for a fix and whether we should failover to our internal fallback.

Thanks,
Sana Patel
Head of ML Product, Novacredit

Attachment: server-log-snippet.txt (text, 12KB)
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
To: Sana Patel <sana@novacredit.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Jul 2028 10:02:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected truncation / token suppression in production (novacredit-prod)

Hi Sana — thanks for the report and the log sample. We’ve opened an incident on the status page and pulled the runtime team into a bridge. Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2028-07-04-transient-output-suppression

Interim actions we’ve taken (visible to Novacredit):
- Detected elevated prefetch/batching pressure in the us-west serve cluster coincident with your spike; we’ve routed new traffic for Novacredit to a warmed fallback backplane (compatible model variant) to avoid the suppressed-path.
- Enabled additional token-level tracing for 1 hour to collect more evidence — this will not change inference semantics.
- If you prefer, you can flip to your internal fallback while we stabilize; we won’t block the switch.

We’re continuing to investigate KV/prefix caching and the prefetch fanout logic as suspected vectors. I’ll follow up with a remediation ETA within 90 minutes. I’ve looped Ben to coordinate any commercial follow-up (credits / SLA).

— Alex
Alex Martinez | Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Sana Patel <sana@novacredit.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Jul 2028 12:47:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected truncation / token suppression in production (novacredit-prod)

Sana — quick ops update from the bridge:

What we saw
- Short, high-concurrency bursts temporarily opened a prefetch fanout path that surfaced an edge-case in our prefilling module. Under that specific sequence, the runtime deferred emission of the last chunk of tokens and returned early. Calls still returned 200.

Customer impact
- A subset (~38%) of generation calls during the window experienced truncated output; model logits were computed but final emission was skipped.

Fix / mitigations completed (12:30 PDT)
- Hotfix deployed: a defensive guard in the prefetch path to ensure emission is flushed after batch completion.
- Novacredit traffic remains routed to fallback pool to avoid any residuals for 2 more hours.
- We collected token traces and are attaching an initial postmortem draft (postmortem-draft.docx) with timeline and logs.

Next steps
- Full postmortem and RCA to be shared by EOD tomorrow (Jul 5).
- Engineering will add a fuzz test for the prefetch/fanout sequences and a regression test in the serving CI.
- Ben will follow up on any contractual / credit questions.

We’re sincerely sorry for the disruption — we know partial outputs are worse than clear failures. Please let us know if you’d like a bridge walkthrough or a live demo of the mitigation.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Incident Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Sana Patel <sana@novacredit.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Jul 2028 15:33:20 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected truncation / token suppression in production (novacredit-prod)

I also want to request a short joint postmortem session where your engineering lead walks our infra folks through the root cause and the regression plan. 30–45 minutes should do it.

Sana
